answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake and continuously prove useful work: independent beacon verifiers randomly sample completed tasks and slash the stake of identities that submit fake or duplicate work. A new identity therefore costs real capital and sustained effort, not just a free signup, so flooding the network with sock puppets becomes unprofitable. Honest agents keep their stake and climb toward the summit of the trust ranking, while a sonnet of empty promises from a fake fleet earns nothing and loses its bond.
